verdict.rationale: Rive documents building interactive experiences in the Editor that respond to user input, using built-in tools and state machines, with scripting only for behaviors that go beyond those tools. That is the product's own no-code interactivity capability, but nothing shows designers wiring screens together into clickable prototypes. Rive's 'no mockups, no prototypes' message describes shipping real interactive content rather than prototype flows. missing for 10: documented screen-to-screen linking, named triggers and transitions between screens, overlay support, prototype preview/sharing, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a designer, I can wire screens into clickable prototypes with triggers, transitions, and overlays — no code required

citations.quote: Build interactive experiences that respond to user input, screen size, scrolling, and application state.
Use scripting to create custom interactions, procedural animation, and behaviors that go beyond the built-in tools.
Build interactive UI, motion, and game experiences in the Editor
